title: Finite etale direct image preserves locally constant modules of finite type
statement: Let $f:Y\to X$ be a finite etale morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-finite-etale-category], let $R$ be a commutative ring, and let $F$ be a sheaf of $R_Y$-modules on the small etale site of $Y$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], where $R_T$ is the constant ring sheaf on a scheme $T$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Suppose $F$ is locally constant of finite type [def-weil-pbc-locally-constant-finite-type-modules]: etale locally it is isomorphic to a constant sheaf with value a finitely generated $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Then the direct image $f_*F$, viewed as an $R_X$-module sheaf [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], is locally constant of finite type in the same sense. No Noetherian hypothesis on the schemes or the coefficient ring and no finiteness of the underlying sets of $R$ or the module values is required.

source.place: Tag 095B, lemma-pushforward-locally-constant, module-sheaf finite-type clause, lines 9972-9991.

proof.text: For each $x\in X$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-etale-local-split] to $f$ and $x$. Obtain an etale neighbourhood $g:U\to X$ with a point over $x$, a finite set $J$, and $Y_U=Y\times_XU=\coprod_{j\in J}V_j$ with each $V_j\to U$ an isomorphism. The neighbourhoods for all $x$ form an etale covering, since their images contain their chosen $x$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Work on each such $U$ separately: neither $|J|$ nor the later constant module values need be independent of $U$.

Put $q:Y_U\to U$ and $h:Y_U\to Y$. The morphism $h$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]. Use literal restrictions of module sheaves as in [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], and write $H=F|_{Y_U}$. For every $W\to U$ in $U_{\mathrm{et}}$, the direct-image formula [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] gives
$$((f_*F)|_U)(W)=F(W\times_XY),\qquad(q_*H)(W)=F((W\times_UY_U)\to Y).$$
The universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies the arguments by $(w,(y,u))\mapsto(w,y)$, with inverse $(w,y)\mapsto(w,(y,w|_U))$. These maps commute with both projections and every $W'\to W$, so applying $F$ gives an isomorphism $(f_*F)|_U\cong q_*H$. Every component is a restriction map of $F$ and is $R$-linear; thus this is an isomorphism of the fixed-coefficient module sheaves. This proves the localization assertion directly, without invoking an abelian-only exchange statement.

Let $s_j:U\to Y_U$ be the inverse of $V_j\to U$ followed by the inclusion of that component, and put $H_j=H|_{s_j}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-direct-image-split-cover-product] with base $U$, source $Y_U$, ring $R$, and sheaf $H$. Its hypotheses are exactly the finite clopen decomposition of Step 1, and its conclusion is the isomorphism
$$q_*H\cong\prod_{j\in J}H_j.$$
The cited statement gives the sectionwise product, including the zero sheaf when $J$ is empty, and does not assume that $R$ is finite.

Each $H_j$ is locally constant of finite type directly from [def-weil-pbc-locally-constant-finite-type-modules]: an object etale over $U$ maps etale to $Y$ through the component (etaleness of compositions follows from [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]), and restricting its covering and trivializations for $F$ gives those for $H_j$. Relocalization is sectionwise restriction [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. On any object $T\to U$, choose a trivializing cover for each of the finitely many $H_j$. Iterated fibre products of these covers give a common covering of $T$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-finite-limits]; this follows by successively pulling back a covering and composing covering families. On each member $W$ all restrictions are constant, say $H_j|_W\cong\underline{M_j}_W$ with $M_j$ finitely generated. The same values remain constant on the refinement by [lemma-constructible-pullback-constant], used for the category of $R$-modules. For $J=\varnothing$ use the identity cover and no module choices.

On any $W$ of Step 4, finite products commute with restriction since both operations evaluate sectionwise (Step 3 and [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]). By [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] a constant module sheaf is the sheafification of its constant module presheaf. The product of the finitely many presheaves with values $M_j$ is the constant presheaf with value $M=\prod_{j\in J}M_j$: its sections are $M$ and all restriction maps are identities. Apply the finite-limit preservation in [lem-weil-pbc-site-r-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact] on $W_{\mathrm{et}}$, with the constant presheaf of rings $R$. It gives
$$\prod_{j\in J}\underline{M_j}_W\cong\underline{\prod_{j\in J}M_j}_W.$$
This is a module-sheaf isomorphism. For the empty family the terminal presheaf of $R$-modules is zero, so the same formula gives the zero constant sheaf.

For each $j$ choose a finite set of generators $m_{j,1},\ldots,m_{j,r_j}$ of $M_j$. The finite collection of vectors in $M=\prod_jM_j$ which have $m_{j,a}$ in coordinate $j$ and zero in the others generates $M$: expand each coordinate of a vector in its chosen generators and sum the resulting coordinate vectors. This is finite generation in [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]; for $J=\varnothing$ the empty set generates $M=0$. Steps 2, 3 and 5 therefore trivialize $(f_*F)|_U$ on the covers of Step 4 with finitely generated module values. Composing those coverings with the covering of $X$ from Step 1 (and restricting to any object of $X_{\mathrm{et}}$) gives exactly [def-weil-pbc-locally-constant-finite-type-modules] for $f_*F$. If $X$ is empty the empty cover suffices. This argument uses no finiteness of the underlying sets of $R$ or $M_j$ and no Noetherian property.

Step 1: lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-etale-local-split, with one neighbourhood per point; these form a jointly surjective cover and the degree may vary. Step 2: elementary localization of f_* through the fibre-product isomorphism W×_U(U×_XY)≅W×_XY with an explicit inverse; R-linearity gives R_U-linearity. Step 3: lem-weil-pbc-direct-image-split-cover-product, whose hypotheses are exactly Step 1's output; it works for any Λ and gives zero for J=∅. Step 4: restriction of trivializations through étale composites, a common refinement from finite fibre products, and lemma-constructible-pullback-constant. That node is in route unit sk-thm-p1 and closed in slopmaster2, so the declared tool_use is harmless and accepted. Step 5: ∏ of constant presheaves is the constant presheaf with value ∏M_j, then clause (2) of lem-weil-pbc-site-r-module-presheaf-sheafification-exact (sheafification commutes with finite limits). Advisory only: \underline M is cited via def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, while the definition uses the module sheafification of def-weil-pbc-constant-coefficient-scalar-extension; the two agree by the standard identification of \underline R-module sheaves with R-module-valued sheaves. Step 6: coordinate generators give finite generation, and composing with Step 1's cover gives local constancy. Edge cases checked: J=∅, X=∅, R=0, ℤ², varying degree, infinite R.
